Yes. GRASP is specifically about grading label-free multi-topic science exams where a student’s several answers are merged into one paragraph, and it uses reference answers encoded in a vector index plus a semantic similarity graph to retrieve and assign the right reference for each question before grading each segment independently [1]. It is the closest match to using a network of reference answers for one long student paragraph covering several questions [1].

The other papers are about rubric-based grading, short-answer grading, synthetic training data, transparency, or broader educational scoring, but they do not describe this multi-question single-paragraph setting with graph-based reference-answer retrieval [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10].
